description: Put a picture or any other file into Passalong and get back the markdown line that points at it. With `file` (a file the user gave you, filled in by the client), it is stored now. Without it, you get a one-time upload link and the curl command that sends the file to it: run that where the file is (a code sandbox, a disk) and its JSON answer has the line. The link works once and expires in 10 minutes; never base64 a file into a tool call instead. If the command cannot reach passalong.dev, the sandbox's network settings block it: tell the user to allow that domain. Accepts image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif; other files up to 10MB. WHERE THE LINE GOES DEPENDS ON WHAT THE FILE IS EVIDENCE OF. Proof that work you are handing in holds (a screen that renders right, a total that matches) goes in that check's `ran` on hand_in, and nothing new is written: a check answered with a picture is shown, which is what the hand-in asks for. A picture that is part of the work itself (the screenshot of a bug, a diagram it explains) goes in its text (create_work, or update_work), because work travels as its text and a file beside it does not travel at all. DO NOT WRITE NEW WORK TO CARRY SCREENSHOTS: six images and a caption each is a hand-in. With `project`, the file is kept in that project instead. Pictures (png, jpg, webp, gif) are drawn where they are named; anything else is a file to download.

file.description: the file the user gave you, filled in by the client

download_url.description: where the file can be fetched (https)

file_id.description: the host's id for the file

file_name.description: original filename, used as the label

kind.description: for an upload link: `image` (the default) for a picture, `file` for a log, PDF, CSV or zip. The link takes only what it was made for

name.description: for an upload link: the filename with its extension, which says what it is

project.description: keep it in this project instead

name: add_file

command.description: the curl command to run where the file is

markdown.description: the line that points at it

upload_url.description: one-time link that takes the file's bytes
